novel_features.name: Morning fleet sweep
novel_features.description: One screen across your whole book of clients. Merges open issues, stale backups, and in-flight DR events into a per-company ranked view, then persists the result so tomorrow's drift command can compare.
novel_features.rationale: Requires three API rollups + local join + ranking + snapshot persistence. No backup vendor's portal shows a single-screen fleet view ranked by attention need.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this in the morning to triage what needs follow-up across every client without clicking through a portal.

novel_features.name: Client QBR report
novel_features.description: Generate the backup section of a client's Quarterly Business Review as Markdown, HTML, or PDF. Job success rate, restore tests run this quarter, coverage map across all three engines, open issues, storage trend.
novel_features.rationale: Every MSP hand-builds these every quarter. We assemble from local store + multiple report endpoints + snapshot history into one executive-grade artifact.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this 1-2 weeks before a client QBR. Saves 30-60 min of manual deck-building per client.

novel_features.name: Drift since yesterday
novel_features.description: Diff two snapshots the CLI collected — show which companies got worse, which recovered, and which are new since a past anchor. Default compares yesterday-to-now on the attention metric.
novel_features.rationale: Trivially impossible without a local time-keyed snapshot store. Every backup portal shows current state; none answers 'what changed since Friday?'
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use Monday morning to start with situation awareness instead of treating every week as a fresh slate.

novel_features.name: Stale-backup follow-up list
novel_features.description: Slice the stale-backup-sets report by company, age window, and backup engine — entirely offline once cached. Use --refresh to repull from the API.
novel_features.rationale: Friday's 'who needs a follow-up?' sweep. Local snapshot means you can filter without burning an API call per slice.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this Friday afternoon to compile the list of clients you need to email about a stalled backup.

novel_features.name: Batch issue triage
novel_features.description: List open issues with filters, then batch-mutate them (ignore / archive / reactivate / comment) in one invocation with --dry-run support and typed exit codes.
novel_features.rationale: The Servosity web portal forces one-at-a-time issue actions. This compresses 20 clicks into one shell command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when the issue queue is bursty or during a planned-outage window where many alerts cluster around one client.

novel_features.name: Restore-queue watch
novel_features.description: Watch every active company's restore queue across the book during a DR event. Polls each company periodically and prints diffs since the last tick.
novel_features.rationale: Web portal forces tab-switching during DR. CLI pins one terminal on every queue at once.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use during an active disaster recovery event when multiple clients have restores in flight.

novel_features.name: Cross-engine backup-facts
novel_features.description: Unified view across Servosity's three backup engines (classic, restic, DR) for one company or all. Engine, ID, hostname, last_successful_at, status, size — joined from three local store tables into one table.
novel_features.rationale: Three API calls become one local query. Cross-engine ranking and filtering is impossible without union-joining the engine tables.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when triaging a client who has multiple engines protecting different devices and you need to know which engine is failing where.

novel_features.name: Bill reconciliation
novel_features.description: Pull the MSP's monthly Servosity bill and compare line-by-line against a CSV of what the MSP is invoicing their clients. Surfaces drift — clients under- or over-charged.
novel_features.rationale: MSP billing reconciliation is the most error-prone manual task per industry research. We do it with integer cents and stable sort.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this every month-end before invoicing clients. Catches missed line items and pricing mismatches.

novel_features.name: Unprovisioned agents
novel_features.description: List agents installed on client machines but not yet pulling backups, ranked by client. Surfaces lost revenue from incomplete onboardings.
novel_features.rationale: Joins the reseller's unprovisioned-agents endpoint with the local companies table to give per-client visibility. Useful onboarding QA loop.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run weekly to catch agents installed during onboarding that never successfully phoned home.

novel_features.name: Storage trend forecast
novel_features.description: Linear-regression forecast of when a specific client will hit a capacity threshold. Reads the historical storage_bytes time series from local snapshots; with --snapshot, persists a new measurement for future runs.
novel_features.rationale: Capacity-needs forecasting requires a time series. Servosity's portal shows current bytes; we project forward to a threshold and surface upsell timing.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run quarterly per high-storage client to identify upsell opportunities before they hit a hard limit.

narrative.headline: The first MSP-fleet CLI for backup. Every Servosity API endpoint as a typed command, plus a local mirror that lets you ask questions the dashboard can't — across your whole book of clients.
narrative.value_prop: No competitor in the MSP backup space ships a fleet-wide CLI. Reach for servosity-msp-pp-cli when you need to triage attention across every client at once, generate the backup section of a QBR in 30 seconds, watch every restore queue during DR from one terminal, or reconcile your Servosity bill against what you're invoicing clients. Every response is agent-native: --json, --select, --csv, --dry-run, typed exit codes.
narrative.auth_narrative: Authenticate with your Servosity partner API token. Export SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN with your reseller-scoped token (find or rotate it in the Servosity partner portal). The CLI auto-resolves your reseller ID from /current-user/ on first run — you never type it.

quickstart.comment: Confirm token works and API is reachable
Pull companies, backups, and issues into the local SQLite mirror
Morning fleet sweep — what needs my attention across my book
Friday review — clients with stalled backups to follow up on
Generate the backup section of a client's QBR as a PDF

troubleshoots.fix: Export SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN with your reseller-scoped token. Get one from the Servosity partner portal.

troubleshoots.symptom: qbr --format pdf returns 'PDF rendering requires Chrome'
troubleshoots.fix: Install Chrome, Google Chrome, or Chromium. Or use --format md / --format html instead.

troubleshoots.symptom: drift returns 'No snapshot found for metric ...'
troubleshoots.fix: Run `servosity-msp-pp-cli attention` first to record the first snapshot, then run drift later to compare.
Run `storage-trend <company> --snapshot` periodically (weekly cron is sensible) to build the trend line.

narrative.when_to_use: Use servosity-msp-pp-cli when you're managing backups across a book of MSP clients on Servosity. It is the right tool for the morning attention sweep, the Friday stale-backup hunt, ad-hoc 'is ACME OK?' checks, batch issue triage during planned outages, restore-queue oversight during DR, monthly bill reconciliation, and quarterly client QBR backup sections. The local SQLite mirror + snapshot history make any 'what changed since X?' question answerable — which the web portal cannot do.

recipes.title: Morning attention sweep with field projection
recipes.explanation: Narrow the output to just the fields an agent cares about — keeps token usage low and pipes cleanly to jq or downstream tools.

recipes.title: Friday stale-backup follow-up list
recipes.explanation: CSV output for paste-into-spreadsheet workflows when you're compiling the list of clients to email.

recipes.title: Client QBR pack
recipes.explanation: Generates a self-contained PDF with cover page, job success rate, restore tests, coverage table, open issues, and storage trend table. Hand it to the account lead 1-2 weeks before the QBR.

recipes.title: Bill reconciliation against invoicing CSV
recipes.explanation: CSV columns: company_id, company_name, invoiced_amount. Output shows delta vs Servosity's bill, sorted by absolute delta — catches under-billing before month-end close.

recipes.title: Restore-queue watch during DR event
recipes.explanation: Emits NDJSON, one tick per line. Pipe to `tee dr-event.log` to capture the timeline of every queue change for the post-mortem.

trigger_phrases: what needs my attention on servosity
show me the QBR backup report for
